newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong gold ends shade down on producer sales.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends shade down on producer sales.

text.p: Hong Kong spot gold ended a shade down on Monday compared to New York's previous close, pressured by producer selling from Australia, dealers said.
Bullion ended at US$327.80/328.30 on Monday compared to New York's previous close at US$328.00/50 on Friday.
With Japanese markets closed on holiday on Monday, gold trading in Hong Kong was relatively quiet, and price gains on shortcovering were erased by producer selling, dealers said.
Australian selling pushed gold down to $327.30/60 per ounce, sparking a brief shortcovering rally in Hong Kong which took gold back up to $328.00 per ounce, they said.
Early European sales in the afternoon pushed gold back down to its closing price, slightly below the day's high.
"Basically the action at the moment is in New York so we're waiting to watch COMEX," said one gold trader.
Physical demand had petered away as prices jumped around US$10 per ounce from levels last week, dealers said.
Traders said that gold would hold above $326 with the top side seen at $332 per ounce.
Local tael gold ended HK$42 up at HK$3,038.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society rose to +0.01 from its previous fix at nil.
